objects.description: Complex number type used by KISS FFT, with real (r) and imaginary (i) parts stored as kiss_fft_scalar (float by default, fixed-point or SIMD depending on compile-time macros).

Opaque handle to the FFT configuration/state object used by kiss_fft APIs. The underlying struct kiss_fft_state is not defined in this header, making this a forward-declared opaque type managed by the library.

Scalar element type used throughout KISS FFT for real and imaginary components. It is a macro-defined type that resolves at compile time to float (default), int16_t/int32_t for FIXED_POINT, or __m128 for USE_SIMD. Included here for completeness, but note this is a macro, not a true typedef; pointer form shown per instructions. Details such as exact size depend on compile-time macros and are unknown from this header alone.

Opaque handle (configuration/context) for real FFT operations in KISS FFT. It is a typedef to a pointer to an incomplete struct kiss_fftr_state, making it an opaque type for users of this API. Used with kiss_fftr_alloc to create, kiss_fftr/kiss_fftri to execute forward/inverse real FFTs, and freed via kiss_fftr_free (macro to KISS_FFT_FREE). The underlying struct layout is not exposed in this header.

Forward declaration of the internal state structure for real FFT plans. Incomplete type; implementation details are private to the library. Users interact with it via the opaque typedef kiss_fftr_cfg.

Opaque handle type for a multi-dimensional KISS FFT plan/state. It refers to an internal struct kiss_fftnd_state defined elsewhere. Used to execute N-D forward or inverse FFTs. Details of the underlying structure are intentionally hidden in this header.

Forward-declared (incomplete) structure that holds the implementation details for an N-dimensional FFT plan in KISS FFT. Not defined in this header; treated as opaque by users and accessed via the kiss_fftnd_cfg typedef.

Opaque handle type for the N-dimensional real-data FFT configuration/state in KISS FFT. It is a pointer to an internal struct kiss_fftndr_state that is not defined in this header, so it is used as an opaque configuration handle for planning/execution of N-D real FFTs (forward/inverse). The lifetime is managed by kiss_fftndr_alloc (constructor) and kiss_fftndr_free (macro to free).

Incomplete forward declaration of the internal state object that holds plan/buffers for N-dimensional real FFTs. Not defined in this header; consumers should treat it as opaque and only use via the kiss_fftndr_cfg typedef and API functions.

functions.name: kiss_fft_alloc
functions.signature: kiss_fft_cfg KISS_FFT_API kiss_fft_alloc(int nfft,int inverse_fft,void * mem,size_t * lenmem);
functions.description: Allocates or initializes a KISS FFT configuration/state for an FFT (forward) or IFFT (inverse). If mem/lenmem are provided, the state may be placed in user-supplied memory; otherwise it is heap-allocated and must be freed by the caller. Usage: call with desired transform length nfft and inverse_fft flag; then pass the returned cfg to kiss_fft or kiss_fft_stride.
requirements: nfft must be a positive integer (>0).
inverse_fft selects direction: 0 for forward FFT; non-zero for inverse FFT (IFFT).
If lenmem is NULL, the function allocates memory internally; the returned cfg must be released with kiss_fft_free (or the corresponding KISS_FFT_FREE).
If lenmem is not NULL and mem is not NULL, then *lenmem must be large enough for the configuration; on success, the cfg is placed in mem and the actual size used is written to *lenmem.

If lenmem is not NULL and (mem is NULL or *lenmem is too small), the function returns NULL and writes the minimum required size to *lenmem; the caller must then provide a buffer of at least that size and call again.
mem, if provided, must point to writable memory of at least the size specified by *lenmem and must remain valid for the lifetime of the cfg.
cfg returned is specific to the nfft and direction requested and must be used consistently with those parameters in subsequent FFT calls.

functions.name: kiss_fft
functions.description: Computes a complex-to-complex FFT (or IFFT if cfg was created for inverse) on nfft samples from fin into fout. Each sample is a complex number (kiss_fft_cpx) with .r and .i components. Intended usage: allocate cfg with kiss_fft_alloc for the desired nfft and direction, then call kiss_fft with fin and fout buffers of length nfft.
requirements: cfg must be a valid configuration returned by kiss_fft_alloc for the intended nfft and direction (forward or inverse).
cfg must not be NULL and must remain valid for the duration of the call.
fin must point to at least nfft elements of kiss_fft_cpx corresponding to the nfft used in cfg.
fout must point to at least nfft elements of kiss_fft_cpx corresponding to the nfft used in cfg.
fin is read-only during the call (declared const).
The transform length nfft is determined by cfg; the caller must ensure input/output buffers match that size.

functions.name: kiss_fft_stride
functions.signature: void KISS_FFT_API kiss_fft_stride(kiss_fft_cfg cfg,const kiss_fft_cpx *fin,kiss_fft_cpx *fout,int fin_stride);
functions.description: Performs a complex FFT/IFFT like kiss_fft, but reads input samples with a stride: the k-th input is fin[k*fin_stride]. Useful when input data are interleaved or when subsampling. Output is contiguous in fout.
requirements: cfg must be a valid configuration returned by kiss_fft_alloc for the intended nfft and direction.
cfg must not be NULL and must remain valid for the duration of the call.
fin must contain at least 1 + (nfft-1)*fin_stride readable elements of kiss_fft_cpx (based on the nfft in cfg).
fout must point to at least nfft writable elements of kiss_fft_cpx.
fin_stride must be a positive integer (>= 1).
fin is read-only during the call (declared const).
The transform length nfft is determined by cfg; the caller must ensure buffers are sized appropriately given fin_stride.

functions.name: kiss_fft_cleanup
functions.description: Releases internally managed memory used by the KISS FFT library. Not required for normal operation, but can be called before program exit to reduce reported leaks or tidy static allocations.
requirements: May be called at program shutdown or after all FFT operations that depend on internal caches.
Must not be relied upon to free user-allocated cfg buffers (those must be freed by the caller).
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unspecified; avoid calling concurrently with other KISS FFT operations.

functions.name: kiss_fft_next_fast_size
functions.description: Returns the smallest integer k such that k >= n and k factors only into 2, 3, and 5 (a size considered fast for this FFT). Useful for padding input to an efficient FFT length.
requirements: n should be a non-negative or positive integer; behavior for n <= 0 is unspecified in this header.
The function is pure (no side effects) and can be called at any time.

functions.name: kiss_fftr_alloc
functions.signature: kiss_fftr_cfg KISS_FFT_API kiss_fftr_alloc(int nfft, int inverse_fft, void *mem, size_t *lenmem)
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a configuration object for real-input FFTs (forward or inverse) using the KISS FFT real-optimized routines. The returned handle is used with kiss_fftr (forward) or kiss_fftri (inverse). If you do not want to manage memory yourself, pass mem = NULL and lenmem = NULL to let the library allocate internally. Details about other allocation modes are not documented here.
requirements: nfft must be even (explicitly stated).
The returned kiss_fftr_cfg must be checked for NULL before use (inferred: allocation may fail).
If mem = NULL and lenmem = NULL, the function will allocate its own memory (explicit).

If providing a memory buffer via mem, lenmem must point to a size value that accurately reflects the available buffer size (inferred from common KISS FFT patterns; exact semantics not documented here).
Use a cfg created with inverse_fft = 0 for forward transforms via kiss_fftr, and inverse_fft != 0 for inverse transforms via kiss_fftri (inferred from parameter name and function pairing).

functions.name: kiss_fftr
functions.signature: void KISS_FFT_API kiss_fftr(kiss_fftr_cfg cfg, const kiss_fft_scalar *timedata, kiss_fft_cpx *freqdata)
functions.description: Computes the forward real-to-complex FFT using a configuration created by kiss_fftr_alloc. Input is real-valued time-domain data; output is the positive-frequency half-spectrum including DC and Nyquist (nfft/2+1 complex bins).
requirements: cfg must be a valid, initialized handle from kiss_fftr_alloc with the same nfft and created for forward transforms (inverse_fft = 0) (inferred).
timedata must point to at least nfft scalar samples (explicit: "input timedata has nfft scalar points").
freqdata must point to space for at least (nfft/2 + 1) complex values (explicit: "output freqdata has nfft/2+1 complex points").
cfg, timedata, and freqdata must be non-NULL (inferred).

functions.name: kiss_fftri
functions.signature: void KISS_FFT_API kiss_fftri(kiss_fftr_cfg cfg, const kiss_fft_cpx *freqdata, kiss_fft_scalar *timedata)
functions.description: Computes the inverse complex-to-real FFT using a configuration created by kiss_fftr_alloc. Input is the positive-frequency half-spectrum (nfft/2+1 complex bins, including DC and Nyquist); output is nfft real time-domain samples.
requirements: cfg must be a valid, initialized handle from kiss_fftr_alloc with the same nfft and created for inverse transforms (inverse_fft != 0) (inferred).
freqdata must point to at least (nfft/2 + 1) complex values (explicit: "input freqdata has nfft/2+1 complex points").
timedata must point to space for at least nfft scalar samples (explicit: "output timedata has nfft scalar points").
cfg, freqdata, and timedata must be non-NULL (inferred).

functions.name: kiss_fftr_free
functions.description: Macro alias for KISS_FFT_FREE; intended to deallocate a kiss_fftr_cfg obtained via kiss_fftr_alloc when the allocator was used internally. Usage: call kiss_fftr_free(cfg) to release resources associated with the FFT configuration. The actual underlying deallocation function and exact parameter type are defined by KISS_FFT_FREE in kiss_fft.h. Details are unknown here because this is a macro alias, not a function declaration.
requirements: Argument should be the kiss_fftr_cfg returned by kiss_fftr_alloc when mem was NULL (inferred from naming and allocation pattern).
Do not pass a buffer owned by the caller when kiss_fftr_alloc was given a non-NULL mem (inferred from naming and allocation pattern).
Call at most once per allocated configuration handle to avoid double-free (inferred from standard resource management patterns).
Behavior, allowed argument types, and NULL-safety are determined by KISS_FFT_FREE in kiss_fft.h; consult that definition (unknown here due to macro alias).

functions.name: kiss_fftnd_alloc
functions.signature: kiss_fftnd_cfg KISS_FFT_API kiss_fftnd_alloc(const int *dims, int ndims, int inverse_fft, void *mem, size_t *lenmem);
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a KISS FFT multi-dimensional (N-D) transform configuration. Call this once to create a plan for a forward or inverse N-D complex FFT given the per-dimension sizes in dims. Typical usage: pass dims (length ndims) and inverse_fft (0 for forward, non-zero for inverse). You may either provide a memory buffer via mem/lenmem or pass mem = NULL to have the function allocate internally (and optionally query required size via lenmem). The returned handle (kiss_fftnd_cfg) is used with kiss_fftnd.
requirements: dims must be a valid, non-null pointer to an array of at least ndims integers representing the size of each dimension (inferred from parameter types and naming).
ndims must be a positive integer (> 0) (inferred from parameter meaning).
inverse_fft selects direction: 0 means forward transform; non-zero means inverse transform (inferred from parameter name and common KISS FFT usage).
If mem is non-null, it must point to a writable buffer of at least *lenmem bytes to hold the configuration (inferred from KISS FFT alloc pattern).
If mem is null and lenmem is non-null, *lenmem may be used on return to report the required allocation size (inferred from KISS FFT alloc pattern).

If mem is null, internal dynamic allocation is used; caller is responsible for freeing the returned configuration with the corresponding KISS FFT free mechanism (typically kiss_fft_free or free, library-specific; exact API not shown here, thus unknown exact deallocator).
The function returns NULL on allocation/parameter failure; callers must check the return value before use (inferred from typical alloc semantics in KISS FFT).

functions.name: kiss_fftnd
functions.signature: void KISS_FFT_API kiss_fftnd(kiss_fftnd_cfg cfg, const kiss_fft_cpx *fin, kiss_fft_cpx *fout);
functions.description: Execute an N-dimensional complex FFT using a previously created configuration. The direction (forward or inverse) and dimensionality are determined by cfg created via kiss_fftnd_alloc. Provide input samples in fin and receive the transformed output in fout.
requirements: cfg must be a valid, non-null configuration created by kiss_fftnd_alloc with the intended dimensions and direction (inferred from API pattern).

fin must be a valid, non-null pointer to an array of complex samples with a length equal to the product of the configured dimensions (exact count inferred; exact layout/stride beyond contiguous array is unknown).
fout must be a valid, non-null pointer to a buffer capable of holding the same number of complex samples as fin (inferred).

Input and output buffers must not overlap unless the library explicitly supports in-place operation; in-place support is unknown from this header, so callers should assume distinct buffers to be safe (conservative requirement due to missing documentation).
The function does not return a status; callers cannot directly detect runtime errors from the function call (inferred from void return).

functions.name: kiss_fftndr_alloc
functions.signature: kiss_fftndr_cfg KISS_FFT_API kiss_fftndr_alloc(const int *dims, int ndims, int inverse_fft, void *mem, size_t *lenmem);
functions.description: Allocates and returns a configuration (plan) for performing N-dimensional real-input FFTs using KISS FFT. The plan is direction-specific, controlled by inverse_fft, and is later passed to kiss_fftndr (forward) or kiss_fftndri (inverse) for execution. If you do not wish to manage the plan memory yourself, pass mem = NULL and lenmem = NULL to let the library allocate internally.
requirements: dims must point to an array of at least ndims integers describing the size in each dimension.
dims[0] must be even (explicitly stated).
ndims should be a positive integer describing the number of dimensions (inferred from parameter purpose).
inverse_fft selects transform direction for the plan: 0 for forward (used with kiss_fftndr), non-zero for inverse (used with kiss_fftndri) (inferred from common KISS FFT pattern and function names).
If you do not wish to preallocate memory for the plan, set mem = NULL and lenmem = NULL (explicitly stated).

If providing a memory buffer via mem, lenmem should be a valid pointer to the size of that buffer in bytes (standard KISS FFT alloc pattern; exact behavior beyond the NULL case is not documented here).
The returned kiss_fftndr_cfg must be non-NULL before being used with execution functions.
The cfg must be freed when no longer needed (see kiss_fftndr_free macro mapping to free).

functions.name: kiss_fftndr
functions.signature: void KISS_FFT_API kiss_fftndr(kiss_fftndr_cfg cfg, const kiss_fft_scalar *timedata, kiss_fft_cpx *freqdata);
functions.description: Executes a forward N-dimensional FFT from real-valued time/space-domain data to complex frequency-domain data using a previously created N-D real FFT plan. Input is an ndims-dimensional real array; output is the corresponding complex spectrum with Hermitian symmetry compressed along the last dimension.
requirements: cfg must be a valid plan created by kiss_fftndr_alloc with inverse_fft = 0 (forward direction) (inferred from naming and typical KISS FFT usage).
timedata must point to at least dims[0] * dims[1] * ... * dims[ndims-1] real samples (explicit dimensionality stated).
freqdata must point to at least dims[0] * dims[1] * ... * (dims[ndims-1]/2 + 1) complex elements (explicit dimensionality stated).
dims[0] must be even (a requirement of the plan; explicitly stated in the header comment for alloc).
timedata and freqdata must be non-NULL and sufficiently aligned for their types (inferred general C requirement).
cfg, timedata, and freqdata must remain valid for the duration of the call; no overlap between input and output buffers is implied or supported (not documented; avoid aliasing to be safe).

functions.name: kiss_fftndri
functions.signature: void KISS_FFT_API kiss_fftndri(kiss_fftndr_cfg cfg, const kiss_fft_cpx *freqdata, kiss_fft_scalar *timedata);
functions.description: Executes an inverse N-dimensional FFT from complex frequency-domain data to real-valued time/space-domain data using a previously created N-D real FFT plan. Input dimensions are the opposite of kiss_fftndr (compressed along the last axis), producing a full real output grid.
requirements: cfg must be a valid plan created by kiss_fftndr_alloc with inverse_fft != 0 (inverse direction) (inferred from naming and typical KISS FFT usage).
freqdata must point to at least dims[0] * dims[1] * ... * (dims[ndims-1]/2 + 1) complex elements (explicit via “exact opposite” of forward).
timedata must point to at least dims[0] * dims[1] * ... * dims[ndims-1] real samples (explicit via “exact opposite” of forward).
dims[0] must be even (requirement originates from the plan; explicitly stated for alloc).
freqdata and timedata must be non-NULL and sufficiently aligned for their types (inferred general C requirement).
cfg, freqdata, and timedata must remain valid for the duration of the call; avoid buffer aliasing.

functions.name: kiss_fftndr_free
functions.description: Convenience macro that aliases the C standard library free. Use it to release memory allocated for kiss_fftndr_cfg (or related internal buffers) when kiss_fftndr_alloc performed the allocation (i.e., mem == NULL). Since this is a macro to free, its behavior and constraints are identical to free; it does not perform any additional cleanup beyond deallocating the heap block.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer to a heap block allocated by a compatible allocator for free (e.g., malloc/calloc/realloc) or a configuration object returned by kiss_fftndr_alloc when mem == NULL.
Do not pass pointers to stack memory, globals, or memory not obtained from the C heap allocator.
Do not call kiss_fftndr_free more than once on the same pointer (no double-free).
It is safe to pass NULL; in that case no action is taken.
If kiss_fftndr_alloc was called with a user-supplied mem buffer, only call kiss_fftndr_free on ptr if that buffer itself was allocated with a compatible heap allocator; otherwise do not free it here.

functions.name: kissfft::kissfft
functions.signature:
template <typename scalar_t>
kissfft<scalar_t>::kissfft(std::size_t nfft, bool inverse)
functions.description: Constructs an FFT plan for complex DFTs of length nfft with the chosen direction (forward if inverse==false, inverse if inverse==true). On construction, precomputes twiddle factors and factorizes nfft into stages for the mixed‑radix FFT. Use this object to later call transform (complex DFT) or transform_real (real-input DFT packing convention as documented).
requirements: nfft must be >= 1 for subsequent calls to transform/transform_real to be well-defined; constructing with nfft==0 leads to an invalid factorization for transform.
inverse selects the transform direction for all subsequent calls on this instance (can be changed later via assign).
Construction is O(nfft) in time and memory proportional to nfft for twiddles and stage tables.

functions.name: kissfft::assign
functions.signature:
template <typename scalar_t>
void kissfft<scalar_t>::assign(std::size_t nfft, bool inverse)
functions.description: Reinitializes the FFT plan to a new length and/or direction, leaving the object in the same state as if newly constructed with those arguments (potentially faster than creating a new instance). If only the direction changes, it conjugates the existing twiddle factors in-place; if the size changes, it rebuilds internal tables.
requirements: Caller may pass the same nfft to only change direction; twiddle factors will be conjugated in-place.
If nfft changes, the operation runs in O(nfft) and replaces internal buffers; any concurrent use of this instance must be avoided.
For valid subsequent transforms, nfft must be >= 1.
This method is not thread-safe with concurrent transform/assign on the same instance.

functions.name: kissfft::transform
functions.signature:
template <typename scalar_t>
void kissfft<scalar_t>::transform(const std::complex<scalar_t>* fft_in, std::complex<scalar_t>* fft_out, std::size_t stage = 0, std::size_t fstride = 1, std::size_t in_stride = 1) const
functions.description: Computes the complex DFT of length N (N is the nfft used to construct/assign the object). The output scaling is such that the l2 norm is multiplied by sqrt(N) relative to the input; applying forward then inverse yields the original input multiplied by N. The additional parameters (stage, fstride, in_stride) are for internal recursion; external callers should use defaults.
requirements: The object must have been constructed/assigned with nfft >= 1.
fft_in must point to at least N complex values accessible with stride in_stride (i.e., element i is at fft_in[i*in_stride]).
fft_out must point to at least N complex values; fft_in and fft_out must not overlap.
stage must be 0 for external calls; fstride and in_stride must be >= 1 (defaults are recommended).
The instance’s direction (forward/inverse) is fixed by construction or the last assign call and determines the sign of exponents and butterfly behavior.
Behavior and performance depend on factorization of N; all work buffers are internal to the instance.

functions.name: kissfft::transform_real
functions.signature:
template <typename scalar_t>
void kissfft<scalar_t>::transform_real(const scalar_t* src, std::complex<scalar_t>* dst) const
functions.description: Computes the DFT of a real input sequence of length 2*N (where N is the nfft of this instance) and packs the N+1 unique frequency bins into N complex outputs using a standard half-complex format: dst[0].real() holds the DC term, dst[0].imag() holds the Nyquist term (k=N), and bins 1..N-1 are stored in dst[1]..dst[N-1]; the remaining half can be obtained by conjugate symmetry. Scaling matches transform(). Requires std::complex<scalar_t> to have the standard layout (true for float/double/long double).
requirements: The object must have been constructed/assigned with nfft >= 1 to produce meaningful output (if N==0, the function returns immediately).
src must point to 2*N contiguous scalar_t values representing the real input of length 2*N; it must be suitably aligned for reinterpret_cast to const std::complex<scalar_t>*.
dst must point to at least N complex outputs (std::complex<scalar_t>) and must not overlap src.

The complex layout and aliasing requirements must hold: std::complex<scalar_t> must be standard-layout such that reinterpret_cast<scalar_t(&)[2]>(z) exposes real/imag parts; this is guaranteed for scalar_t in {float, double, long double} with std::complex<scalar_t>.
The instance’s direction (forward/inverse) is fixed by construction or last assign; scaling is the same as transform().

data_types.description: An uninterpreted byte blob with no required structure or encoding. The bytes are consumed to fill numeric buffers (scalars or complex components) or memory blocks by direct byte-wise copying or simple per-byte transformations. Any sequence of bytes of any length (including empty in some stubs, though several require non-empty) is valid input; no formatting such as text, JSON, base64, or specific headers is expected.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
import itertools

# This generator produces arbitrary binary data suited for KISS FFT fuzzing stubs
# that consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR blobs to populate real/complex buffers or size
# external allocation requests. We bias outputs to be non-empty and to include
# diverse patterns (zeros, small ramps, sinusoids, impulses, alternating bytes)
# to exercise different FFT behaviors, while remaining valid arbitrary byte data.

_MAX_SIZE = 4096


def _pack_floats(vals):
    # Pack list of floats into bytes (little-endian IEEE754)
    return b"".join(struct.pack('<f', v) for v in vals)


def _make_impulse(length, amp=1.0, pos=0):
    v = [0.0] * length
    if length > 0:
        v[pos % length] = amp
    return v


def _make_ramp(length, start=-1.0, stop=1.0):
    if length <= 0:
        return []
    if length == 1:
        return [start]
    step = (stop - start) / (length - 1)
    return [start + i * step for i in range(length)]


def _make_alt(length, a=-1.0, b=1.0):
    return [a if (i & 1) == 0 else b for i in range(length)]


def _make_sine(length, freq=1.0, phase=0.0, amp=1.0):
    import math
    if length <= 0:
        return []
    return [amp * math.sin(2.0 * math.pi * freq * (i / float(length)) + phase) for i in range(length)]


def _bytes_from_ints(ints):
    return bytes(b & 0xFF for b in ints)


def _repeat_to_size(data: bytes, size: int) -> bytes:
    if not data:
        return b"\x00" * size
    if len(data) >= size:
        return data[:size]
    reps = (size + len(data) - 1) // len(data)
    return (data * reps)[:size]


def _mk_external_mem_block(rng: random.Random, min_sz=64, max_sz=2048) -> bytes:
    # For stubs that use FUZZ_PARAM_STR size to decide external mem buffer length
    # we generate a block header describing a requested size, followed by payload.
    want = rng.randint(min_sz, max_sz)
    # Prefix with a small header encoding the desired size in LE to give variability
    hdr = struct.pack('<I', want)
    # Fill payload with a mix of patterns
    patterns = []
    patterns.append(bytes([0] * min(32, want)))
    patterns.append(_bytes_from_ints(range(256)))
    patterns.append(_bytes_from_ints([0x55, 0xAA] * 128))
    payload = b"".join(patterns)
    payload = _repeat_to_size(payload, want)
    return hdr + payload


def _mk_real_signal_blob(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a real-valued signal (float32) then return bytes; stubs may treat as arbitrary bytes
    # Choose composition of several components to increase variety
    components = []
    # Impulse
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        pos = rng.randrange(max(1, length))
        amp = rng.uniform(0.25, 1.0)
        components.append(_make_impulse(length, amp=amp, pos=pos))
    # Ramp
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        components.append(_make_ramp(length, start=-1.0, stop=1.0))
    # Alternating
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        components.append(_make_alt(length, a=-1.0, b=1.0))
    # One or two sinusoids
    nsin = 1 + (0 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 1)
    for _ in range(nsin):
        freq = rng.randint(1, max(1, length // 4))
        phase = rng.uniform(0.0, 2.0 * 3.141592653589793)
        amp = rng.uniform(0.2, 1.0)
        components.append(_make_sine(length, freq=freq, phase=phase, amp=amp))

    # Sum components and soft clip
    out = [0.0] * length
    for comp in components:
        for i, v in enumerate(comp):
            out[i] += v
    # Normalize to [-1,1]
    mx = max(1e-9, max(abs(v) for v in out))
    scale = 1.0 / mx
    out = [max(-1.0, min(1.0, v * scale)) for v in out]

    return _pack_floats(out)


def _mk_complex_blob(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    # Interleave real/imag float32 pairs, suitable size for kiss_fft_cpx arrays if interpreted
    re = _mk_real_signal_blob(rng, length)
    im = _mk_real_signal_blob(rng, length)
    # de-interleave as (r,i) pairs of float32
    # re and im are both 4*length bytes
    out = bytearray()
    for i in range(length):
        out += re[4*i:4*i+4]
        out += im[4*i:4*i+4]
    return bytes(out)


def _mk_small_blob_set(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a concatenation of multiple blobs to satisfy multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    pieces = []
    # External mem size hint
    pieces.append(_mk_external_mem_block(rng))
    # Real buffers for kiss_fftr forward/inverse (nfft up to 1024 in stubs)
    nfft = 2 * (1 + rng.randrange(1, 513))  # even in [2, 1026], close enough
    nfft = min(1024, max(2, nfft if nfft % 2 == 0 else nfft - 1))
    pieces.append(_mk_real_signal_blob(rng, nfft))
    # Half-spectrum complex for inverse path: nbins = nfft/2+1
    nbins = nfft // 2 + 1
    pieces.append(_mk_complex_blob(rng, nbins))
    # N-D complex arrays seed
    nd_len = rng.choice([16, 36, 64, 125])
    pieces.append(_mk_complex_blob(rng, nd_len))
    # Bytes pattern slice for generic fillers
    patterns = [
        bytes([0] * 64),
        _bytes_from_ints([0x55, 0xAA] * 64),
        _bytes_from_ints(range(256)),
    ]
    rng.shuffle(patterns)
    pieces.extend(patterns)
    blob = b"".join(pieces)
    return blob[:_MAX_SIZE]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Randomly choose one of several generation strategies
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.25:
        # A compact, highly structured blob focusing on real FFT
        nfft = rng.choice([64, 128, 256, 512, 1024])
        blob = _mk_real_signal_blob(rng, nfft)
        blob += _mk_external_mem_block(rng)
        return blob[:_MAX_SIZE]
    elif choice < 0.5:
        # Complex-focused content for N-D and inverse paths
        n = rng.choice([9, 17, 33, 65, 129])
        blob = _mk_complex_blob(rng, n)
        blob += _mk_external_mem_block(rng)
        return blob[:_MAX_SIZE]
    elif choice < 0.75:
        # Mixed content set to satisfy multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumers
        return _mk_small_blob_set(rng)
    else:
        # Generic diverse bytes combining patterns and float payloads
        parts = []
        parts.append(_bytes_from_ints(range(256)))
        parts.append(_bytes_from_ints([0x00, 0xFF] * 256))
        parts.append(_mk_real_signal_blob(rng, rng.choice([128, 256, 384])))
        random_tail = rng.randbytes(rng.randrange(64, 256)) if hasattr(rng, 'randbytes') else bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(rng.randrange(64, 256)))
        parts.append(random_tail)
        blob = b"".join(parts)
        return blob[:_MAX_SIZE]
